quantifiers.original: A given algorithm works over the strongly convex class and induces an algorithm working over the convex class.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For each fixed parameter tuple and phi, next,update,s0 are fixed before the all-g hypothesis and before the all-f conclusion.
quantifiers.evidence: hs quantifies every eligible g and every qualifying minimizer w; its witnesses must equal execution of the same callbacks and s0. The correction is defined before f is quantified and depends only on original callbacks and known u,delta. Neither z nor w is passed into execution. Thus this is actual class-uniformity at the fixed parameter tuple, not selection of a new solver per objective.

assumptions.original: A class solver has the stated strongly convex accuracy and iteration guarantee.

assumptions.evidence: The premise is stronger in specificity than informal source iteration notation: it fixes natural-valued phi, ceiling semantics, deterministic callbacks and successful execution. Source smoothness is represented by an explicit gradient-Lipschitz interface, with the broader source-model adapter left open.

constant_dependencies.original: Substitute the regularization and smoothness parameters in the original solver budget.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: delta=epsilon/R^2; declared regularized smoothness 2beta; q=2beta/delta=2beta R^2/epsilon; logarithmic ratio exactly 2.
constant_dependencies.evidence: hsmall yields delta<=beta, so beta+delta<=2beta. The solver is invoked for the declared 2beta class, not evaluated at a smaller argument followed by a monotonicity claim. Positive R and epsilon justify both cancellations. Natural phi(q)>=0 and log 2<=1 imply ceil_nat(phi(q)*log 2)<=phi(q) using an integer upper bound, including phi(q)=0. No monotonicity or hidden constant is used in this theorem.
